aboutBlurb:
Texoma Storm Shelters provides life-saving storm protection for families and businesses throughout Sherman, Denison, and North Texas. We engineer and install FEMA-compliant above-ground safe rooms, underground bunkers, and in-garage shelters designed to withstand catastrophic EF5 tornadoes.

With North Texas facing frequent severe convective storms, our mission is to ensure every household has accessible, certified severe weather protection. Explore our above-ground safe rooms or review our storm shelter cost guide.
areaBlurb: We proudly serve homeowners and businesses across Grayson, Fannin, and Cooke counties, including Sherman, Denison, Pottsboro, Whitesboro, Van Alstyne, and Gunter.
contactBlurb: Complete residential installations range from $4,500 to $9,500 before the Grayson County 50% grant rebate. Contact us today for a free on-site assessment.

faq.q: How does the Grayson County Safe Room Rebate work?
faq.a: The Grayson County Office of Emergency Management provides a 50% matching rebate up to $3,000 for approved FEMA-certified storm shelter installations. Applications must be submitted and approved before installation begins.

faq.q: Are above-ground safe rooms as safe as underground shelters?
faq.a: Yes. When engineered and anchored in accordance with FEMA P-320 and ICC-500 standards, above-ground steel safe rooms are impact-tested to withstand direct 250 mph EF5 tornado winds and flying debris missile strikes.

Most residential above-ground safe rooms and in-garage floor shelters are installed in a single day (typically 4 to 6 hours). Outdoor underground concrete units typically require 1 to 2 days including excavation.

faq.q: Do I need a building permit in Sherman or Denison?
faq.a: Yes. The City of Sherman and City of Denison require building permits and final anchor inspections for storm shelter installations. We handle the permit paperwork on your behalf.

faq.q: What happens if debris blocks the shelter door?
faq.a: All our safe rooms feature inward-swinging steel emergency escape doors with heavy internal sliding deadbolts, as well as secondary emergency air vents and multi-point emergency release latches.

faq.q: How much does a certified storm shelter cost in North Texas?
faq.a: Standard residential safe rooms range from $4,500 to $9,500 depending on dimensions and capacity (typically 4 to 12 person capacity). With the $3,000 county rebate, net homeowner costs can be as low as $2,250.
